c6b0b16eaf.source: Retailers lose millions every year to inventory inaccuracy. Phantom stock. Shrink. Units that should be on the floor, but aren't. RFID hardware promises to solve this, but hardware alone is just data with nowhere to go. What you need is the software that turns every tag read into a real operational decision. No middleware layer, and hardware-agnostic, so the readers and tags are yours to choose.

8f914884ca.source: RFID provides the signal. We turn it into action.

fdbdb839cb.source: Hold an RFID tag up to the light. You can see it: a set of fine lines, that's the antenna, connected to a tiny chip. That chip stores a number, permanently. No battery required. It just needs a burst of energy from an RFID reader, a gun, a pad, a scanner, to wake up and transmit its ID.

39e0b490b6.source: That ID is an Electronic Product Code

c6e035a7f0.source: Unlike a barcode, which identifies an item that can have many units, an EPC identifies a specific unit of the item.

b76a7fb1b5.source: Say you have ten identical shirts on a shelf: one UPC, but ten different EPCs. Scan them all at once, and that's your count of ten, instantly.

6549e31adb.source: Place your units in a bin and the cart appears on screen automatically. Readers inside the bin blast the tags with energy, capture each EPC, and the system builds the transaction. Again, instantly.

9115893203.source: Follow a single unit through every step that touches it.

2072761e7f.source: Verified at both ends, by unit

3b44eb63fe.source: Scanned in one pass, basket to receipt

0133a573f0.source: The journey starts at the loading dock. Units arrive either pre-tagged at manufacturing, or they are tagged here, a process called commissioning. Each tag is printed, applied, and linked directly to the exact unit being received.

8ce745fc93.source: A portable RFID scanner captures every EPC in the shipment at once

53721b4c6d.source: Our system cross-checks what was expected against what actually arrived, at the unit quantity level

619c392a93.source: Just verification from the very start

69c9592a55.source: Bluebird RFID sled readers with iPhones running the Teamwork Commerce RFID app

9c62882a46.source: As inventory moves between locations, RFID lets us track the exact units transferred. Targeted RFID-reading captures only the units directly involved in the transaction, so nearby stock isn't accidentally included.

34484b4105.source: Our system verifies each EPC at both the source and the destination of the transfer, recording the full movement history

41e2692bcf.source: Instead of guessing, retailers have a clear, unit-level audit trail

1e3e5bbb7d.source: The kind of confidence in inventory data that enables smarter replenishment decisions across stores

922a9ab5c2.source: Whether checkout is handled by staff or by the customer.

fa2ee842c0.source: Instead of scanning each unit's barcode one by one, everything is placed on a read zone and accurately identified instantly. In a staff-led environment, units are read at once, the cart is built automatically, and your team stays focused on service and recommendations.

8ebe80f174.source: In self-checkout, customers place their units in the read zone. All units are identified instantly, the cart is built, and the customer is guided through seamlessly: no lines, no waiting

57182e54c4.source: Either way, same result: faster checkout, accurate receipts, and accurate real-time inventory

ccec65c4a3.source: In high-traffic environments, stadiums, or anywhere there is high-volume retail, we have the ability to enable an RFID-powered bag check at exit. When a customer scans their bag, the system instantly cross-references every EPC inside against their receipt.

e5d26a1913.source: Confirming matches, and flagging anything that does not belong

55f3835247.source: It can also trigger a receipt printout right at the exit, freeing up the checkout for the next customer

5ffd9d87df.source: Instead of alarms that don't tell you who or what triggered them, teams get unit-level precision, and customers can keep moving

f8a5fa1e7b.source: Hours with a large team, or minutes with a single person.

06c0657c05.source: After units have been received, moved, and sold, RFID stock counts verify that everything is where it should be. Counts work by capturing all visible EPCs within range of the reader. Teams can scan the store, covering entire departments in seconds.

4cbd2e5a7b.source: What used to take hours with a large team can now be completed in minutes with a single person

9572151026.source: Instead of periodic snapshots that often get skipped, inventory can be continuously verified

bd94a9f98f.source: A living, always-current picture of what's in stock

c5df91a261.source: A real-time database of which unit is where.

7069c335fe.source: Every action, receiving, transferring, selling or counting, maintains a record of exactly where every unit is, across the entire company. This is the Unit Control Ledger: a real-time database of which unit is in which location, when it moved, and where it's supposed to be.

45905199d5.source: If a stock count reveals a discrepancy, an adjustment is recorded directly, and that adjustment is also logged on the ledger

727ac04230.source: The result is a single source of truth for every unit in your inventory, from the moment it enters the store to the moment it leaves

2e1bf3cfd9.source: What makes Teamwork Commerce RFID different from competitors?

8ea208acf4.source: Teamwork Commerce offers a native RFID stack that runs from tag commissioning at receiving through transfers, counts and checkout. No third-party middleware required, and the reader hardware is yours to choose. Our RFID is native to the core logic: every transaction (receiving, counting, transferring, selling) operates by individual EPC, not just UPC.

bceca4b350.source: What hardware do you support?

557d7d9259.source: We publish a certified hardware list covering the devices integrated and supported with TW POS Pro, including Bluebird RFID handhelds. It is deliberately short, roughly one certified device per category rather than a catalogue, and there are no certified EAS gates on it today. We recommend certified hardware for full compatibility; if you want to use something not on the list, your Client Success team can advise on support.

7edde18fa9.source: Can vendors pre-tag items, or do we need to commission tags in-store?

fbcec735e1.source: Both. If your vendor or warehouse ships goods already tagged, they scan straight into the purchase receipt. If not, Teamwork provides an integrated encoding workflow inside the purchase receipt document: define quantity, print and encode tags, affix them, then RFID scan to populate the receipt with individual EPCs. One step, no separate process.

Teamwork Commerce gives you the whole journey, from the moment a unit arrives to the moment it sells, and everything in between. One platform. Connected data. Unit-level visibility at every step.
